question_text: Jerry Seinfeld, the American stand-up comedian and star of NBC's Seinfeld, wrote a book titled X, published in 1993. Written as his television show was first rising in popularity, it is primarily an adaptation of his stand-up material. The title comes from an article in Entertainment Weekly, listing the numerous catchphrases for which the show was responsible. X was critically acclaimed and scored a spot on the New York Times Best Seller list. Hint: The title is a pun.

In 2003, X - an American Actress and Singer, filed a $50 million lawsuit against photographer, Kenneth Adelman, and Pictopia.com for 'breach of privacy' to suppress an aerial photograph of her Malibu mansion. Prior to the lawsuit, the photograph had been downloaded only six times, two of those being by X's attorneys. Following the lawsuit, more than 420,000 people viewed the photograph over a month. This led to the term 'X Effect' being coined, to describe a situation where an attempt to hide, remove, or censor any information results in increasing public awareness of the information. ID X.

X is a European Capital located around 320 km south of Munich, 477 km east of Zürich, and 124 km west of Zagreb. The city's symbol is a Dragon (X is also called the City of Dragons), the origin of which lies in a Slavic myth that claims that the slaying of a dragon releases the waters and ensures the fertility of the earth. It is thought that the myth is tied to the marsh that lies south of the city, and periodically threatens X with flooding. ID X.

X is a famous dessert whose name literally translates to "Pick me up" or "Cheer me up". An X World Cup is held every year where ordinary foodies from around the globe compete to create the best X. In his latest stand up set, Kanan Gill recounts his experience of participating in this World Cup. ID X.

Donna Andrews is an American mystery fiction writer, and author of the award-winning Meg Langslow series - a blacksmith from Yorktown, Virginia (also the author's hometown) who's an amateur sleuth. All the novels in the Meg Langslow series feature a bird-based pun in the title: some examples, Owls Well That Ends Well (2005), Stork Raving Mad (2010), Toucan Keep a Secret (2018), Murder Most Fowl (2021), among others. What was the title of the fifth book in this series, the title of which may remind you of a famous line of dialogue from the 1942 film, Casablanca?

___ ____ _________ is a fashion trend that spawned from a series of viral Tiktok videos in 2024. The first viral video that kickstarted the trend was posted on January 6, 2024, when a 28-year-old Canadian blockchain product developer named Kayla Trivieri shared a video declaring: "Clean girl is out; ___ ____ era is in, okay?" The aesthetic is characterized by its maximalist approach, and emphasizes opulence, luxury, and confidence. The most important accessories are leopard print garments, faux fur, knee-high boots, oversized sunglasses, and chunky gold earrings. What is this fashion trend that got a nod from Francis Ford Coppola himself?

In 2006, a French luxury fashion brand sued a Las Vegas based company, Haute Diggity Dog, for trademark infringement with their collection of furry dog toys, X (two words). The brand claimed that since they also makes some of its own pet products, the toys are likely to cause confusion. The case was dismissed and the Court ruled it as a clear case of parody of the products from the French fashion company. Haute Diggity Dog, whose product line included items like "Chewnel No. 5" and "Dog Perignonn", continues to produce the X collection to this date. ID X.

X is a South American city that lies in the valleys of the Andes. X is notable for a unique urban transit system of aerial cable cars called Mi Teleférico ("My Cable Car") that opened in 2014. Historically based on a site of a former Inca City, the name X literally translates to "The Peace". ID this city located in the country where Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid were killed in a shootout.

Inside Man is a 2006 American crime thriller film, directed by Spike Lee and starring Denzel Washington and Clive Owen. The film centers on an elaborate bank heist-turned-hostage situation on Wall Street, and begins with Clive Owen's character, Dalton Russell, proclaiming he has committed the perfect bank robbery. As his monologue ends, the credits start to roll over a famous 90's Bollywood song. ID this iconic song that is in the soundtrack of Inside Man.

X is a brand of frozen waffles owned by Kellanova, and sold in North America. It was invented in 1953 by the American inventor Frank Dorsa, who developed a process by which waffles could be cooked, frozen, and packaged for consumers. In 2016, the Netflix series Stranger Things featured X as a key story theme bringing the brand to global attention beyond the countries where the brand is sold. In the show, they are the favorite food of the character Eleven. ID X.

Nino Rota was an Italian composer who was nominated for Best Original Score for The Godfather. The nomination, however, was rescinded when the Academy discovered that the "Love Theme" from the film was a rewritten version of Nino Rota's music from the 1958 film Fortunella. The theme was lyricized in English by Larry Kusik into "Speak Softly, Love", a popular song released in 1972. The music was also copied and adapted into a Bollywood song from the 90's. ID this Bollywood song.
answer_text: Raja Ko Rani Se Pyaar Ho Gaya

question_text: X was an American actress with a career spanning six decades as a Hollywood leading lady. Known for her headstrong independence, spirited personality, and outspokenness, she cultivated a screen persona that matched this public image, and regularly played strong-willed, sophisticated women. X holds the record for the most acting Oscars by any performer, male or female, with four Academy Awards for Best Actress, a benchmark yet to be breached. ID X.

The 1974 film, The Great Gatsby, starring Robert Redford in the titular role, received the Oscar for the Best Costume Design. While Theoni V. Aldredge, credited as the Costume Designer, won the award, the credits of the film also list "Clothes by _____ ______" for his contribution to the menswear in the film - shirts, ties, and suits for Redford, which helped crystallize the film's clean, pastel-leaning 1920s menswear image. ID this American fashion designer, best known for founding the eponymous fashion brand.

Böcker Maschinenwerke GmbH is a family-owned manufacturer of lifting technology based in Werne, Germany. The company was in the news this month for leveraging a real-life incident in a social media post. The post accompanied a picture of the said incident, with a slogan in German that translates to, "When something needs to be done quickly." The post also highlights their product's ability to transport up to 400 kilograms of "your treasures" at a speed of 42 meters per minute. And it moves "whisper quiet" thanks to its 230 Volt E-Motor, the post says. ID this real life incident.

X is an American company based in Venice, California, that delivers its products to customers by mail. On March 6, 2012, the company uploaded a YouTube video entitled "Our ______ Are F***ing Great" featuring CEO Michael Dubin, delivering his speech in a nonchalant and sarcastic manner. The video prompted 12,000 orders in a two-day span after it was released, and has received over 28 million views to date. In 2016, X was acquired by Unilever for a reported $1 billion. In October, 2023, Unilever sold a majority stake in the company to Nexus Capital Management, while still retaining 35% of X. ID X that got famous on the back of its viral campaigns.

Only three films have ever won all the "Big Five" Academy Awards - Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actor, Best Actress and Best Writing. The second one to do so was One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest in 1975, and the third was The Silence of the Lambs in 1991. Which 1934 Romantic Comedy film, directed by Frank Capra, was the first one to achieve this feat?
